thread:
sasha: Heads-up: while updating SDK snippets I found the 429 guidance in the error ref is risky. It shows immediate retries without checking Retry-After.

ben: Oof. Which file?

sasha: docs/error-reference/429-behavior.md. The curl and python examples need to prefer Retry-After header, then our X-Redwood-Retry hint, then fall back to exponential+jitter.

kai: Agreed. I'll draft a compact python SDK pattern and a short shell/curl example that parses Retry-After (with a note that the one-liner is brittle).

sasha: Please include a tiny repro script QA can run to simulate a surge and observe 429s, plus a short checklist for triage.

ben: Checklist should include: confirm model fallback policy, check autoscale status, look at per-route latency/queue metrics, and inspect upstream proxies for extra rate-limits.

kai: Also add streaming guidance: on interrupted streams prefer reconnect with backoff and reattach partial state when safe.

sasha: For the retry logic add normalization: treat Retry-After < 1s as 1s minimum and apply +/-30% jitter. Call out not to retry indefinitely (use circuit-breaker).

kai: Will open a small PR under docs/error-reference and add SDK snippets under docs/sdk-snippets/python, js, go. Title: "429 playbook: Retry-After-aware retry examples".

docs-bot: PR created by kai: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/pull/900 \ Labels: docs, 429-playbook, needs-approval.

sasha: Reviewing now.

ben: Quick nit: show both header precedence and fallback to model switch (smaller model) as an example.

kai: pushed changes per feedback. deploy-bot: staging build queued.

deploy-bot: preview published at https://docs-preview.redwood.com/429-playbook-retries.

sasha: Merged after tiny wording fixes. Thanks everyone. Thread resolved.
